newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish stocks edge higher in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish stocks edge higher in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted minor gains in range-bound and thin trade on Friday as the lack of fresh cash entry continued to depress the market, brokers said.
"The index was stuck in a narrow range between 63,000 and 63,800 points. Investors did not want to take positions ahead of the weekend," said Haldun Sertel from Can securities.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed 213.66 points, or 0.34 percent higher at 63,438.84 after retreating from an early high of 63,860. Trade volume eased to 5.6 trillion lira from Thursday's 5.7 trillion.
Over the week, the index lost 1.7 percent after last week's 0.7 percent drop.

The market had recovered 1.48 percent on Wednesday after diving three percent in the first two days of the week due to worries over Iraq's military drive in northern Iraq, followed by U.S. missile attacks on military targets in southern Iraq in retaliation.
Brokers said there was need for more cash entry to overcome the 63,800 barrier which the market failed to pierce for the second time after Thursday.
They expect trade to be squeezed in narrow ranges unless major developments on the Iraqi front occur.
Turkey spelled out limited military goals inside northern Iraq, saying its troops had yet to cross the border and insisting a planned security zone would be only temporary.

The 85-share industrial index .ISEI gained 0.22 percent to 69,681.51 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF firmed 0.66 percent to 56,011.42. Of the 221 shares traded, 77 rose, 71 fell and 73 finished unchanged.

The most active stock was department store chain Carsi Magazacilik which made up 12 percent of the total daily volume, losing 1,000 lira to close at 27,000. -- Aydan Eksin, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 0875.
